reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies in the temporal and spatial trade-off between crashing and retreating. The Crash Index (CI) aggregates aggressive offensive positioning, while the Retreat Index (RI) captures defensive preparation. CI > RI suggests a team prioritizes rebounding over defense, whereas RI > CI indicates defensive dominance. The transition defense efficiency (TDE) formalizes this as a ratio of successful defensive transitions to rebound opportunities. The failure mode occurs when teams misjudge timing—crashing too late or retreating too early—leading to suboptimal outcomes. The mathematical structure reveals a dynamic equilibrium where optimal strategy balances CI and RI to maximize TDE. Empirical validation uses 2011–2012 NBA data to correlate CI/RI with actual rebound rates and defensive success.
